clue.text: Fashion that is some con when differently cut

parts.note: to fashion something is to make it

indicators.note: the letters are put together differently, so they are rearranged

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a fashion is a bit of a con when it is cut a different way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges SOMECON plus IE (from 'that is') into ECONOMIES; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise is to cut spending, so the phrase is a synonym for cut back.

clue.text: Out 24 24 out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the referenced word are knocked out of order

parts.note: 24 refers to the other light of the linked answer, VOTE in the phrase put it to the vote

explanation.surface: A terse, repetitive slogan about voting.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Out' rearranges VOTE, the word 24 supplies; '24 out' is read as 'vote out'.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto a proposal is to reject it, in effect voting it out.

clue.text: Drive away from Soho?

indicators.note: from, with the question mark, tells us the letters are made from Soho shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about being driven out of Soho, a London district known for nightlife.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is a district of central London; its four letters, rearranged, give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To shoo a cat or bird is to drive it away with a gesture or cry.

clue.text: One dips in at random but there's little of taste

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: the letters are put in no particular order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dips into a dish at random and finds it bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at random' scrambles the letters of 'dips in', placed after the Roman numeral for 'One'; 'but' is a link and the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insipid is bland, lacking flavour.

clue.text: Bemused saint came to con elusion things were meant to be thus

definitions.text: things were meant to be thus

indicators.note: a bemused saint is confused, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: came to a conclusion means ended

explanation.surface: A puzzled holy figure reaches a verdict that all happened according to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bemused' scrambles the letters of 'saint'. 'con elusion' is a printing slip for 'conclusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: As planned: something done the way it was meant to be done.

clue.text: Nick, there's no problem! Relax!

parts.note: a reassuring word to a friend called Nick, telling him not to worry and to calm down

explanation.surface: A friend reassures a worried Nick.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means relax and not exert oneself, as a calming instruction.

clue.text: Sourpuss taking Edward round city district mistrusted him

indicators.note: sour suggests the cat's letters have gone off and turned into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
EC is the postal district of the City of London
Ted is a short form of Edward

explanation.surface: A grumpy person, out with Edward, comes to distrust him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sourpuss' splits as 'Sour' (the anagram signal) and 'puss'; EC is the London postcode area for the City, the financial district; 'taking' and 'round' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To suspect someone is to mistrust them, doubting their honesty.

clue.text: See 6
Bobbie's peepers?

parts.note: a bobby is a British police officer, and peepers are eyes, so this means the police watching

explanation.surface: A playful question about a policeman's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: A bobby is slang for a British police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: The police watching people are figuratively the gaze of law enforcement.

clue.text: See 1
Upset heavyweight with close-cut hair

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer upset over a crew cut.
explanation.walkthrough: NOT, also spelt NOTT, is an old word for close-cropped or hornless.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adjective for cropped short, as in nott-headed.

clue.text: Nose put out of joint for ages

indicators.note: a nose put out of joint is broken, so its letters are disarranged

explanation.surface: Someone has had their nose put out of joint for a very long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out of joint' rearranges NOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aeons are vast periods of time, so 'for ages' is a casual equivalent.

clue.text: Late thought added about a ballet step

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: PS, postscript, is a late thought added to a letter

explanation.surface: A dancer adds an afterthought about a dance move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts PS round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pas is the French ballet term for a step.

clue.text: A dumb show of family. entertainment

definitions.meaning: a performance in mime with no words
a Christmas stage show for the whole family

explanation.walkthrough: A panto is a British Christmas stage show for families. The full stop after 'family' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Mime is wordless acting; a British panto is a seasonal family theatre show.

clue.text: When there's dissension ask supporters to raise arms?

definitions.text: When there's dissension ask supporters to raise arms?

parts.words: When there's dissension ask supporters to raise arms?
parts.note: raising arms is a show of hands, the way a divided meeting settles matters

explanation.surface: Advice for a quarrel that sounds like a call to violence.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputed question is settled by ballot, with supporters lifting their hands.

clue.text: One is never sorry to have them!

definitions.text: One is never sorry to have them!

parts.words: One is never sorry to have them!
parts.note: reads as something nice to own, but means having nothing to be sorry about

explanation.surface: A remark about something welcome to own.
explanation.definitionFit: Being never sorry means feeling no remorse at all.

clue.text: Once more the cause of profit tax?

definitions.meaning: tax is levied on what comes over and above a gain, read whimsically

explanation.definitionFit: Again means anew; the second reading splits the phrase as above a gain, which is what gets taxed.

clue.text: Appeal to Turkish governor to carry out order

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in O help us
a bey was a governor in the Ottoman Empire

explanation.surface: Someone petitions an Ottoman official to have a command executed.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with an order is to do as told.

clue.text: Rattles around hoping for a lead

indicators.note: around means the letters are moved round into a new order

explanation.surface: Something shakes noisily as someone waits for a lead role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges RATTLES.
explanation.definitionFit: A young actress hoping for a starring role is an aspiring film star.

clue.text: In short, Saturday duty fixed for doing homework?

indicators.note: fixed means repaired or rearranged, so the letters are put in new order

parts.note: Sat is the short form of Saturday

explanation.surface: A weekend chore is arranged for a pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges SAT and DUTY together.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil at their books is engaged in study.

clue.text: Cover up a single occasion in a U S state

indicators.note: in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
once means on a single occasion

explanation.surface: A cover-up happened just once in an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts one piece inside the other; Cal is an old abbreviation for California.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to cover it up.

clue.text: Male returning guns

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Male returning guns' with no count: GAT reversed gives TAG, but 'Male' does not define it and 'guns' is plural; the clue appears garbled

clue.text: A holy guide should put CID on the right road

definitions.text: A holy guide should put CID on the right road

parts.words: A holy guide should put CID on the right road
parts.note: CID is the British detective branch; a helpful clue sets detectives on the right track

explanation.surface: A religious guide is supposed to keep detectives on the straight and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: A useful clue in an investigation points police the right way.

clue.text: See 8
A paper somewhat bedraggled?

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the word is used, so the letters are found within it

explanation.surface: A newspaper looking rather the worse for wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is slang for a low-quality newspaper.

clue.text: See 13

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'See 13' held with answer OYE, which does not fit: the linked light should be VOTE, completing 13-down

clue.text: A Highlander sounds feeble when stylish punters meet, of course

definitions.text: when stylish punters meet, of course

parts.note: a Highlander is a Scot from the Scottish Highlands

indicators.note: sounds means we take the word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: feeble means weak

explanation.surface: A Scotsman seems weak during a fashionable race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Ascot is a fashionable English horse-racing meeting held each June; 'of course' puns on racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The week of racing at Ascot racecourse draws smart racegoers.

clue.text: The business centre in local government ownership

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the words that follow it

explanation.surface: A commercial centre owned by the local council.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters spanning the end of 'government' and the start of 'ownership'.
explanation.definitionFit: A town centre is where shops and businesses cluster.

clue.text: Wickedness from 5's first four

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Wickedness from 5's first four' refers to 5, whose first four letters (ASIN) do not give EVIL; the cross-reference is broken as held

clue.text: Talkative bird from down under

parts.note: a noisy parrot native to New Zealand

explanation.surface: A chatty Antipodean bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' means Australia and New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: The kaka is a New Zealand parrot, and parrots chatter.

clue.text: Huts get demolished accordingly

indicators.note: demolished huts are knocked down and rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: Sheds are knocked down as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get demolished' rearranges HUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean in this way or consequently.

clue.text: The tot is tidy, there's nothing to add

definitions.text: The tot is tidy, there's nothing to add

parts.words: The tot is tidy, there's nothing to add
parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirits; tidy means neat, and nothing added means no water or mixer

explanation.surface: A remark about a tidy child that needs no further comment.
explanation.walkthrough: A tot is a small measure of spirits, not only a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotch served with no water or ice is described as neat.
